authorship: Slean example; not a UCI or Capital Bikeshare protocol
question: Does the 2011 hour-of-day mean lower 2012 hourly demand MAE by at least 5 bikes/hour versus the 2011 global mean?

source.attribution: Fanaee-T, H. (2013). Bike Sharing [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5W894

historical_time.timezone: not specified by source; retain date and hour labels without UTC conversion

split.order: strict chronological holdout; never fit on 2012 rows

target.meaning: total rental bikes in each recorded hour

baseline.prediction: arithmetic mean of cnt over all 2011 hourly rows

candidate.prediction: arithmetic mean of cnt among 2011 rows with the same hr; use the 2011 global mean only if that hour is absent

metric.definition: MAE(global mean on 2012) minus MAE(hour-of-day mean on 2012)
metric.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic from integer counts; round each displayed MAE and the final improvement to 6 decimal places with ROUND_HALF_EVEN

cpu_budget.coverage: open pinned local ZIP member, parse CSV, fit both 2011 means, predict and score 2012; exclude network fetch and result serialization

stop_rule: Exactly one evaluation on the 2012 holdout, no tuning and no retry chosen by outcome.
limits: Retrospective teaching comparison on one public dataset; no operational, causal or scientific validity claim beyond the computed sample.
